answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake compute inside a trusted execution kernel that signs every action with a hardware-bound key, so identities cannot be cloned cheaply. Reputation then accrues as a slow thread of verified work, like a comet leaving a long tail: each completed task appends one attestation, and trust only grows after sustained honest history. A fresh attacker spawning thousands of identities starts with zero tail, so their votes and trades carry no weight until they pay the same real time and compute cost as everyone else.
